words.en: That bias set has not been proposed for adoption, so there is nothing to adopt yet. A set is written, then proposed, then adopted — and the middle step is what stops a set becoming binding without anybody having offered it.
words.note: bias' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: Nothing was adopted, because no reason was given. Adopting a lens changes how this team reads evidence, so the record keeps, beside your name, why you are adopting it. Say why in a sentence or a short paragraph (at most 2,000 characters) and adopt it again.
words.note: bias' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: Nothing was added, because this one has already been settled — by the lens moving back, by a re-run under the lens now in force, or by a member who gave their reason. What settled it is on the record and is not overwritten. If the lens changes again, the obligation is raised again as a new one.
words.note: bias' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: Nothing was settled. This was asked by a machine credential, and saying that a lens change does not affect a finding is a person's judgment about the work — not something an automated account can decide on anyone's behalf. A machine may raise this and show it to you; answering it is yours.
words.note: bias' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: Nothing was settled, because this request has no member behind it. Deciding that a change in the team's declared lens does not affect a piece of work is somebody's judgment, and the record keeps whose it was. Sign in and do it as yourself.
words.note: bias' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: Nothing was settled, because no reason was given. The whole of what this act puts on the record is why you judged that the change in the lens does not bear on this work — without it the record would say only that somebody decided, and a later reader could not tell whether the question was answered or waved away. Say why, and it is settled.
words.note: bias' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: Nothing was settled, because the request did not say which piece of work it is about. A bias debt belongs to one assistant run — the one whose lens changed — so settling it has to name that run.
words.note: bias' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: Nothing was settled, because there is no open bias debt on that run here. Either the run never carried one, or it has already been settled, or it is not a run you can open.
words.note: bias' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: Nothing was settled, because the reason given is longer than this record holds for one. Nothing about it was wrong — it is a size limit and not a judgment about what you wrote. Put the reasoning where it belongs in the work and give the short form of it here.
words.note: bias' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: Reading a policy proposes a bias set; it never adopts one. Adopting is something a member does with their name on it, because otherwise a team could say it follows an organization's standards without anybody in the team having agreed to anything.
words.note: bias' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: A pattern statement is a claim about how an institution actually behaves, so it is analysis and needs evidence in the record. It can be written in draft without one; it cannot leave draft without one.
words.note: bias' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: That bias set was not written. One or more of its statements is not something the record can honor, and each one is named below with what is wrong with it. Nothing was saved, so nothing needs undoing — correct the statements and write it again.
words.note: bias' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: This bias set is adopted and does not say what it does NOT check. A case held to a standard has to say which parts of that standard this system verifies and which it does not — the parts that can be counted are rarely the parts that protect, and enforcing only the countable half while staying silent would carry the authority of the whole policy without its substance.
words.note: bias' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: That statement assigns a truth value to a source wholesale, and declared bias may never issue verdicts. It may raise scrutiny, it may block an inference, and it may assert a pattern it can evidence. The construct that fights undeclared distortion is held to a higher standard than the distortion, so this is refused whoever declares it.
words.note: bias' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: That is a standard of evidence — how strong support must be before you assert it — and a standard is a BAR rather than a lens. Declare it as your project's required strength, where it will actually refuse work that falls short. Filed here it would refuse nothing, because a declared bias is disclosed and never gates.
words.note: bias' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: One of these bias statements is missing something the record needs to apply it: a stable name, one of the three kinds it can be, or the sentence itself. The three kinds are raising scrutiny on a source, blocking or licensing an inference, and asserting an evidenced pattern — a standard of evidence is not one of them; that is a bar.
words.note: bias' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: That statement does not say why the lens is held. A declared bias the system honors is one its author justified; without that it is an unstated prior with a form around it.
words.note: bias' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: That statement names its subject in prose rather than pointing at the subject registry. Registry entries are what let the record notice when a project statement and a team statement are about the same thing — in prose, nothing can tell, and a collision that is quiet is the one this construct exists to prevent.
words.note: bias' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: A phase starts after, or a judgment leads to, a phase of the same scenario, or a matter the plan is about. The one named is neither. Nothing was written.
words.note: action-plans' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: A new measurement cannot re-grade the documents already read by that engine, and that holds even when the new measurement is WORSE. What the record does instead is name exactly which transcriptions were graded under the old measurement, so a person can look at them and decide. Grades in this record are things people put their name to.
words.note: calibration's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: Nothing here was actually measured. A release note, a changelog, a model card or a new version number all tell you an engine CHANGED — none of them tells you how well it now reads a page, and that is the number the record grades against. Run the probe and record what it scored, including the inputs you gave it, so somebody else can disagree with you later.
words.note: calibration's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: This measurement is not readable as one. It has to name an engine, a version, a date, and the probe run that produced it — and the quality figure, where there is one, has to be on the same scale the rest of this record uses.
words.note: calibration's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: This announcement carries a quality figure. Noticing that a vendor announced something is useful and the record keeps it — it brings the next check forward. But what they say about their own product is a claim, and a grade in this record rests on a measurement. The announcement cannot stand in for the check, and it cannot change a grade on its own.
words.note: calibration's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: This announcement is not readable as one. It has to say which engine it is about and where you saw it, because it is somebody else's statement about their own product and the record keeps it attributed to them.
words.note: calibration's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: To put an engine on the calibration schedule you have to say which probe will check it. Registering measures nothing yet, but a schedule with no stated way of measuring is a promise nobody could keep, or tell was kept.
words.note: calibration's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: To put an engine on the calibration schedule you have to say which engine. Registering it measures nothing yet — it only says what will be checked, and so it has to name it.
words.note: calibration's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: This measurement does not say who ran it. A measurement is something somebody did, and a later reader who doubts the figure needs to know whose it is to ask for it to be run again.
words.note: calibration's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: A measurement has to carry the day it was taken. How good an engine is, is a fact about a particular day — without one, nothing can tell whether anybody has checked recently, and nothing can ever supersede it.
words.note: calibration's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: A measurement has to say exactly what it measured — which engine, and which version of it. Services are retrained and re-released under the same name, so the name alone cannot tell a later reader whether the thing you measured is the thing that read their document.
words.note: calibration's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: This capture could not be recorded as belonging to anybody in particular, so it was not made. An act that names one party where two acted reads as though a person did something a machine did, or the other way round, and that is worse than a missing document.
words.note: capture-requests' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: The site this would fetch from has asked us to slow down, or has refused us recently, and we are waiting the interval it named. The request is still queued and will be made when the wait is over — nothing has been lost and nothing needs re-asking.
words.note: capture-requests' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: Every request your team's Civicsmith makes says what it is for, so a source can tell a first capture from a routine re-check and throttle one without blocking the other. This one names a purpose that is not one of the things it could truthfully be doing.
words.note: capture-requests' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: This round of fetching has already been to that site once. Requests are spread out rather than sent in a burst, so this one waits for the next round. It is still queued.
words.note: capture-requests' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: Your team's Civicsmith will not fetch without saying who is asking and how to reach whoever is running it. Being refused honestly is a fact that can be recorded; being admitted by disguise is a claim that could not be defended later.
words.note: capture-requests' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: This request asked to fetch as the member's own browser, and the record does not hold what that browser is. Presenting an agent nobody actually used would be inventing a client rather than speaking as one, so it asks rather than guessing.
words.note: capture-requests' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: Your team's Civicsmith tried to fetch the document and the fetch did not land, so nothing was captured. That says nothing about the document or the site beyond this one attempt, and it is recorded as a look that could not tell. The request is still queued and is tried again on a later round, until it expires.
words.note: capture-requests' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: The record already holds this document, under another record. A document has one home in the record — the first record that registered it — and registering it again here would move it away from there. Nothing was written. Cite the record that holds it, or, if you found it at a new address, that sighting is already recorded as a corroboration of the one it holds.
words.note: provenance's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: The record lists this document, but keeps it in parts rather than as one file, and your team's Civicsmith has no record of fetching it itself. A timestamp is only requested for bytes your team's Civicsmith can vouch for, so none was requested. Nothing is missing: do not capture the document again. If your team's Civicsmith fetches it from its address, it can then be co-attested.
words.note: attestation's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: This mark could not be made or withdrawn. Marking a site as a platform that asks for a login is a member's own act, and it names one site by its plain host name, such as www.example.org. Nothing was written.
words.note: capture-requests' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: The assistant may read anywhere while it searches, but it asks to capture only an address the record already holds: one a held document was captured from, or one a held document links to, exactly as written, its query and anchor included. This address is not one of them, so nothing was queued or fetched.
words.note: capture-requests' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: This web address is longer than 2,048 characters, the most a capture request may carry. A longer one is refused whole, never cut, because a shortened address would name a different page. Nothing was queued or fetched.
words.note: capture-requests' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: A request asks for a document; it never brings one. The fetch is performed by your team's Civicsmith itself so that where the bytes came from is something the record established rather than something it was told, and a provenance chain anybody could hand us is one anybody could invent.
words.note: capture-requests' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: The choice about a public archive copy reads co_archive: true (ask for one), false (ask for none), or nothing to let the team's setting decide. This request sent something else. Nothing was queued.
words.note: capture-requests' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: Whether a capture also asks a public archive to keep a copy is a member's choice, or else the team's setting. This request was not made by a member, so it cannot choose. Nothing was queued.
words.note: capture-requests' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: This names the same question twice — the one being worked, and the one the document supposedly bears on. Evidence for the question you are already working is just evidence for it, and flagging it as belonging somewhere else would put a note in front of you saying a document you just asked for is about something other than what you asked.
words.note: capture-requests' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: This says the document bears on another question, but what it names is not a question. The whole point of noting a lead is that somebody working that question will be told about it, and there is nobody to tell if it does not name one.
words.note: capture-requests' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: A capture is requested under a question, and the thing named here is not one. The question is what the request is accountable to, and a fetch belonging to nothing is a fetch nobody can later account for.
words.note: capture-requests' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: What was asked for is not a public web address. What an investigation session may reach is what anybody could reach by typing it into a browser, so an address that is not public on its face is not asked for at all.
words.note: capture-requests' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: This request cannot be asked again. Only a request the source itself turned away, under a question you can see, goes back into the queue; a request that is still waiting, was captured, has expired, or was refused for any other reason does not. Nothing was changed.
words.note: capture-requests' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: This request did not name the piece of work asking for it, or named one that is not running here. Every fetch your team's Civicsmith makes on its own is traceable to a session somebody opened, because that opening is what authorizes it.
words.note: capture-requests' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: This request names a step of work that is not one you can see here. A request made for a step is tied to it, so the step it names must be one its asker can see; one that does not exist answers the same. Nothing was queued.
words.note: capture-requests' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: This asked for the page as a visitor would see it in a form your team's Civicsmith does not recognize. It reads render: true, or nothing at all for the document as the site serves it, so a request for the rendered page is never quietly turned into a request for the page's empty frame. Nothing was queued.
words.note: capture-requests' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: This request described the site it asks for in a way your team's Civicsmith does not recognize. It reads site_kind: "personal" for a private person's own site, "platform" for a page on a platform that asks for a login, or nothing for an ordinary public page. Nothing was queued.
words.note: capture-requests' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: The site turned this request away: it asked for a login, a payment or a different browser, or refused for another reason it gave. Nothing was captured. A member who can see the question may supply what the site asked for and ask again.
words.note: capture-requests' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: This request asked to be filed under a sweep, and that sweep does not take it: the sweep is not ratified, is held, or does not reach this address. Nothing was fetched or filed under it. A request filed under a sweep answers to what members ratified for that sweep, so it is never stretched to fit.
words.note: capture-requests' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: An option's category is one of: mitigation, legal, awareness, journalistic, grassroots, other. Nothing was written.
words.note: action-plans' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: That checkpoint has already been judged. Nothing was written.
words.note: action-plans' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: That checkpoint is not due yet: its phase has not started, or its days have not passed. Nothing was written.
words.note: action-plans' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: A judgment names a scenario of the plan, one of its phases that has a checkpoint, whether it was met or not met, and a note of up to 500 characters. Nothing was written.
words.note: action-plans' translation, keyed by its code; B411 E1: plain words

words.en: A claim is a quoted part of one of the interview's answers, or your own words. Quote it exactly as it stands. Nothing was written.
words.note: investigation's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: A claim is found through its "find the record" step. Make that step first, then tie the record to it. Nothing was written.
words.note: investigation's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: Say what the public body is remembered to have said or done, in at most 2,000 characters. Nothing was written.
words.note: investigation's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: A project closes as resolved, superseded or abandoned. Nothing was written.
words.note: investigation's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: A closing note on what the team would do differently is at most 4,000 characters. Nothing was written.
words.note: action-plans' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: Choosing which mention of a subject is the one on point for a connection is a member's own act, done in their name. A machine may point out the mentions a document holds, but deciding which one a connection rests on is a judgment a person signs for.
words.note: connections' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: The mention named is not one this document carries for that subject. The choice is among the places the record actually read the subject in this document, by the reference as the reading recorded it; a mention the record never read cannot be the one a connection rests on.
words.note: connections' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: That request does not name a connection this record holds and you can see. A connection is named by the two documents it joins and the subject that joins them, and it exists once the record has derived it — choose after it appears among the document's connections.
words.note: connections' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: That reference was read at more than one place in this document, and each place is its own mention. Say which one is on point — by the occurrence the record lists for it, or by the place as the record names it — and the choice will rest on that place alone.
words.note: connections' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: This document mentions the same subject in more than one place, and the record linked the two documents through the strongest-graded mention without anyone choosing which mention is the one on point. Because another mention bears on the part you cited, whether this connection reaches your citation is undetermined rather than yes or no. A citation of the document as a whole is answered today; a member may also choose which mention is the on-point one for this connection, and the answer then follows that choice.
words.note: connections' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: This record holds no passage with that address, so there is no part of a document whose connections could be weighed. A content address is minted when a citation first points at a passage — if you expected one here, the citation that would have made it has not been written yet.
words.note: connections' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: This connection was established by a reference somewhere else in the document, not in the part you cited. A citation that points at a passage stands on what is IN that passage, so it cannot borrow a link the record found elsewhere in the same file. Cite the part where the reference actually appears, or cite the document as a whole and say so.
words.note: connections' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: The record knows which reference links these two documents but not where in either document it was read, so it cannot say whether that reference falls inside the part you cited. This is stated rather than assumed either way: the connection is real and its reach into your citation is undetermined until the document is read with positions.
words.note: connections' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: That consent cannot be recorded: the detail it names is not in this source's history, or consent to a wider audience already stands. Nothing was written.
words.note: sources' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: What a copy says of itself is recorded with the passage of its text that says it. None was named, or it is not one of the standard's passages. Nothing was written.
words.note: standards' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: A captured copy is official, a codifier's, the copy in force, a draft, superseded, produced in answer to a records request, a vendor's model, or not known. This one names none of these. Nothing was written.
words.note: standards' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: A regulated date is written year-month-day and names its basis: the statute, order or commitment that sets it. Nothing was written.
words.note: action-plans' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: The version of the declared flow this decision names is not the one standing now. Rather than file your decision against a description you did not read, the record keeps it out and asks you to look again: read the question against the version in force and decide again. The answer may well be the same one, and it will then be yours. Both versions are named beside this message, the earlier one still reads back in full, and nothing was recorded.
words.note: progressions' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: A disposition is one of: open, chosen, declined, done, blocked. Nothing was written.
words.note: action-plans' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: That edition is already withdrawn, and a withdrawal is never repeated or lifted. Nothing was published.
words.note: docket's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: That entry is already settled: placed in public, declined, listed as received, or taken back. A later entry says what changed. Nothing was written.
words.note: docket's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: The entry's kind is not one the docket takes, or does not fit who it is from: a response or a statement comes from the subject or someone granted standing, a reaction from anyone else, and an outcome from anyone. Nothing was written.
words.note: docket's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: An unsealing order names a part that no sealing order on this case's docket names. Nothing was published.
words.note: docket's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: Every docket entry says who it is from: the case's subject, someone granted standing, or the source's name, in at most 200 characters. This one names nobody. Nothing was written.
words.note: docket's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: Only a joined participant of the case's project files to its docket. Nothing was filed.
words.note: docket's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: Only an owner of the case's project manages its public docket. Nothing was published.
words.note: docket's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: The entry says it is from the case's subject, and the one it names is not a subject of the edition named. Nothing was written.
words.note: docket's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: A reaction elsewhere links to an independent archive's copy, and this capture has none. Ask for the archive copy again, then place it. Nothing was published.
words.note: docket's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: Every docket entry has a captured copy with its origin, and the capture named is not one this record holds with the address it came from. Capture it first. Nothing was written.
words.note: docket's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: Every docket entry names the edition of the case it concerns, and the edition named is not one this case has published. Name a published edition. Nothing was written.
words.note: docket's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: Your team has no name recorded yet, and a docket entry is never anonymous. Record the team's name first. Nothing was published.
words.note: docket's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: Say, in your own words and at most 2,000 characters, why, and choose whether the entry is for the record, for the public docket, or both. Nothing was written.
words.note: docket's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: The entry relies on a grant of standing that is not in force: it was never made on this case's docket, or it has ended. Nothing was written.
words.note: docket's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: A summary is one paragraph of at most 600 characters: a reaction elsewhere is shown with one in the team's own words, and an outcome is filed with one in yours. Nothing was written.
words.note: docket's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: A court order is placed with what it orders (remove, redact, seal or unseal), the published editions it names, and, to redact, seal or unseal, the parts of the edition it names. This one does not say so. Nothing was published.
words.note: docket's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: This docket entry is already marked as a threat; a mark is never rewritten. Nothing was marked.
words.note: docket's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: The signature is not a valid signature of this docket entry by one of your own registered signing keys, for the reason named. Nothing was published.
words.note: docket's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: Your team's Civicsmith holds no prepared docket entry from you with this fingerprint, it was prepared more than an hour ago, or the docket has moved since. Prepare it again and sign what it shows. Nothing was published.
words.note: docket's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: A take-back is never itself taken back. Place the entry again if it should stand. Nothing was published.
words.note: docket's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: A public docket entry is permanent: a later entry can take it back but never unsay it, and posting it says you have read that. Nothing was published.
words.note: docket's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: A withdrawal is never taken back. To stand behind the case again, publish a new edition. Nothing was published.
words.note: docket's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: A reaction goes only under reactions elsewhere, and every other public entry only on the listed shelf. Nothing was published.
words.note: docket's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: The check of that Google Drive document did not run: the export address said it was sending a document and sent a web page instead. Your team's Civicsmith reads the bytes rather than the label, so the application page was recognized and not compared against the captured document — comparing it would report a change on every visit that nobody made.
words.note: monitoring's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: The check of that Google Drive document did not run: the export address answered with a web page rather than a document, which is what Drive does when a file stops being shared with anyone who has the link. Nothing was compared and nothing about the record changed — what is known is that your team's Civicsmith could not see the document today.
words.note: monitoring's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: The same document is placed at the same step twice in this request. Place it once. Nothing was written.
words.note: progressions' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: Two steps of this flow share one key, so a document placed at that key could belong to either. Give each step its own key. Nothing was written.
words.note: progressions' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: A find is accepted by a member, as found, edited, or set aside for her own. Nothing was recorded.
words.note: question-explorer's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: A find is gauged as supporting the question, cutting against it, or unclear, with a short account of how. Nothing was offered.
words.note: question-explorer's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: The system can offer only a capture, a passage or a connection the record holds and the paying account may see. Nothing was offered.
words.note: question-explorer's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: You take part in a project drawing on this question, so a find is dismissed there, for the project. Nothing was recorded here.
words.note: question-explorer's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: No exploring run by that name is open for this caller. Nothing was done.
words.note: question-explorer's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: No find by that name was offered to you. Nothing was recorded.
words.note: question-explorer's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: This exploring run has read as many pages as it may. It stopped where it was.
words.note: question-explorer's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: An exploring run looks at no more than 20 people. This one reached that number, so it stopped and its step was set aside.
words.note: question-explorer's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: The system looks at a person only when a member has tied that person to the question. This look was not made, and the exploring goes on without it.
words.note: question-explorer's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: This document is kept away from the assistant, so the system did not read it.
words.note: question-explorer's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: This exploring run has ended. Nothing was done.
words.note: question-explorer's translation, keyed by its code

words.en: A member confirms, corrects or disputes a local fact; this act is none of the three. Nothing was written.
words.note: local-facts' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: Say how you checked, in at most 500 characters: the official page and its address, a call to the office, a visit. None was given, or it is too long. Nothing was written.
words.note: local-facts' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: A correction gives the corrected value, in the form the profile holds that fact in, and its source in at most 500 characters. The value is missing or not of that form, or the source is missing or too long. Nothing was written.
words.note: local-facts' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: The series named for this standard is not one your team's jurisdiction profiles list. Name a series they list, or none. Nothing was written.
words.note: standards' translation, keyed by its code

words.en: This provision already has a confirmed force, which the answer names. Withdraw it, with your reason, before recording another. Nothing was written.

civicsmith.org
Civicsmith's own website: what it is, a team's published work, the teams that chose to be listed, and how to start a team.
Create your Civicsmith team
Creates your team's Civicsmith in a Cloudflare account your team controls: what you need, a permanent short name, Cloudflare's permission, then your one-time password.
Update your team's Civicsmith
Updates your team's Civicsmith to the signed release chosen in Settings › Updates, and no other. Records, members and settings are kept.
Your team's page
Your team's own page: who it is, what it has published, how to hand it material and how it works, with members' sign-in beside it.
How we work, step by step
How your team works, in six short steps, for anyone: no account needed, nothing recorded.
Choose a new password
Choose a new password from the one-time reset link an administrator made for you.
Forgot your password
How to get back in without email: use one of your recovery codes, or ask an administrator for a one-time reset link.
Set up your team's Civicsmith
The first administrator's setup: claim the installation, then name the team, choose its places and languages, and decide how members reach the assistant.
Who your team is
What kind of team yours is, what it focuses on and why it exists. It shapes how members are welcomed and locks nothing.
Your invitation
Your invitation to join a team. Choose your language, the name the team will know you by, and a password.
Your team's home
Your team's home, the nerve center: what needs you, what needs the team, every area at a glance, the projects and what changed since you last looked. Start here each day.
Members
Everyone in your team and what each may do. Administrators invite members, set what they may do, and see who holds the hosting account.
Security
Administrators only: how hard your team's Civicsmith is being tried, by kind and by hour, against its own usual. Counts only; nothing names who tried.
Your account
Your own settings: your handle, password, signing key, language and expertise.
The assistant
Whether and how the assistant serves you: on your team's key, your own Claude account, or not at all. Set your limit and suggestions here.
The team's assistant
Administrators only: the team's API key, what it pays for, its limits, its use summed over members, and keeping the team's material away from AI.
Declared bias
The lens your team reads evidence through, stated so a reader can discount it. Write a set, draft one from an outside policy, adopt it, and settle work made under an earlier lens.
Places and offices
Administrators only: the places whose rules your team's Civicsmith follows (deadlines, holidays, offices, records laws), and the offices and seats your team deals with.
Recovery codes
Your own recovery codes, which let you set a new password if you lose yours. Each works once.
Your team
Administrators only: your team's name, website, languages, what a court can reach, who holds the hosting account, and its bar.
Settings
Every setting in one list: yours first, then the team's.
More
The places the tabs below do not hold: projects, people and settings.
Updates
Administrators only: the release your team's Civicsmith runs, the release ready to install and what changes in it, and the choice: Update, Not now or Skip this version.
Your ties
Your own ties to people or organizations the team may look into. Only you and the administrators see this list.
Your notes
Your private notes. Only you can see them in your team; turn one into an observation, a hunch or a question when you choose.
Translations
The words members see, in your team's languages. Members given the grant translate them, the assistant drafts where it can, and protected words are checked twice.
Wizards
Step-by-step walk-throughs of the real screens. Civicsmith's own come with each release; your team can write its own or copy one and change the copy.
Projects
Every project you can see: its stage, who works on it, how busy it is, and when it last changed.
Themes
The team's themes: lenses that gather documents and passages, never evidence.
The Action dashboard
The Action area as a dashboard: clocks and whose move it is first, then what needs you, then every action.
A project's dashboard
One project as a dashboard: your next steps here, the project at a glance, its story so far, and its activity.
Can't open this
What you see when an address leads nowhere, when something isn't yours to see, or when your team's Civicsmith can't be reached.
Where else to go
What you see when what you need is not Civicsmith's work: the places your team's place lists for it, each with what it does, how to reach it and where that came from. Opening it records nothing.
Your queue
Your queue: everything waiting on you, in one list. To do needs your act, Noticed is something new nobody has judged, and Status tells you where something stands.
Find
Find what your team holds, or look outside for something it doesn't yet. Capture what you find into the record.
Add
Add something to the record: a document from its address, a file, or what you saw yourself, in your own words.
Held captures
Captures waiting for a member to vouch for them before they enter the record. Release them, or set them aside with a reason.
Archive
One captured archive and every file in it: which are filed and held for review beside it, which were already held, and which were not filed and why.
Opening a file
Before a file opens: whether it is low or high risk and why, its safe view, the checks it has had, and how a held file is released.
Document
One document as captured: its words by page, its copy's grade, its versions beside each other, the links it carries, the people and organizations it names, and what cites it. Cite from here.
Two documents in tension

Two passages in your team's record that are in tension: see both as written, then settle it by saying how they differ or that one is wrong, take it up as a question, conclude it, or dismiss it as a lead.
Find in this

Look through a document, the documents you are holding together, or a project for people, money, dates, requirements or a word. Each result shows its passage; you record what matters with the usual act.
Project
A project: its questions, their strength against the project's bar, its members and its stage. Open a question or a plan from here.
Objective
AI for this project
Question
One question: what supports it and what cuts against it, its strength against the bar, and what would change the answer.
Ask
Ask in plain words, with the assistant, or find and count without it. Answers come only from what your team holds, and show where they looked.
The assistant panel
A question with the assistant beside it. It answers only from what your team holds and never concludes, signs or sends.
People
The people and organizations your team's record follows, those named in your projects first, each with how often the record names them. Your own members are under Settings › Members.
Person
A person the record follows: positions over time, what they decided and signed, each fact dated and cited.
Timeline
What happened, in order: the city's acts and your team's acts in two lanes, never mixed. Undated items are listed apart.
Money trail
A money trail: figures from budgets and reports, each with its stage and period, included or left out with a reason.
Calculation
A calculation shown with its method and inputs, each tied to the record and recomputed when an input changes.
Help: How a records request works
What the law requires of the office you ask for records, the faster request, and what the city's portal shows.
Help: How spot-checks work
A help page: one of Civicsmith's methods explained in plain words, opened from the screens where it is used.
Explore connections
Chains of connections between people, votes, contracts and payments, each step cited and graded. A chain is a lead until a member cites its documents.
Proceeding
A court case or legal proceeding: its parties, its register of filings, and orders with their reply dates.
How this date was worked out
One due date and how it was worked out: the law or commitment it comes from and how the days were counted.
Standard
A standard the city set itself, held from its document, that questions can test the city against.
Action plan
An action plan: the options for what to do about a problem, the order to try them, and what each waits on.
Start and send
Start an option from a plan: prepare what is sent, check who it goes to today, and send it after the warning.
Glossary
What the terms and marks in the record mean, in plain words: money terms, how the record is kept honest, and what each state allows.
Start an action
Start an action of any kind: who it goes to, what it asks, how carefully to act, what it rests on, and when it is due and why.
Request records
Ask an office for records under the law that requires it to answer. The due date is worked out for you.
Action
One action your team took: what was sent, to whom, when a reply is due, and what came back.
Litigation hold
Where a legal threat reached the team and what it keeps because of it: any member who can see the action or the case places a hold, with a reason.
Hold notice
The notice that tells members what to keep outside Civicsmith. You send it yourself; Civicsmith records that you did and nothing about anyone else.
Brief counsel
A packet for the team's lawyer: what the record holds on one action, as it stands, for a claim or for a defense. It is never published or filed.
Your team's own rules
A deadline or a legal fact your jurisdiction's profile lacks, drafted by one member and applied only after another member confirms it.
Matter
A matter: what the team is pursuing about one problem, from the first letter to the outcome.
Case
Prepare a case for publishing: its scope, statement, findings, the people it names and why, its timeline and what it leaves out.
Review copy
A draft case shared with named outside readers before publishing. Their comments come back here.
Publication ceremony
The publication ceremony: the last checks, then signing. Publishing is permanent; corrections come as a new edition.
A review copy, from outside
What someone outside the team sees when asked to review a draft case: the draft and a place to comment.
Published case
A case your team published, as anyone reads it: findings, their strength, the evidence, and how to check it without the team.
Another team's case
Another team's published case, recreated here. Nothing in it counts for your team until a member accepts it with a reason.
Docket
The public record of every edition, correction and withdrawal of your team's cases.
A case's docket, from outside
Lets anyone check what happened to a published case after it was published, without an account. Your team files and posts its entries on its own Docket.
Inbox
Material handed to your team through its doorbell. Move it into the record, or discard it with a reason.
Hand material to the team
Hand material to the team. You need no account; the page says what will happen to what you send.
A source
Leads
Write down something you were told, record who looked into it and what they found, and share it with a project.
Watched addresses
Every address your team watches: what is due to be checked, pausing the watching, and the sweeps that look through a site.
Public registers
The public registers your team holds: bring one in whole, search it and cite a row, watch a filer, license or docket by its number, and connect outside alerts.
AI providers
The team's AI: the accounts in use in order, budgets and alerts, the seven privacy and origin checks, what members may use, and the catalogue of providers and their plans.
Connect an AI
One plan, connected step by step: what it is sent and which terms bind your use, signing up, giving the key, what you accept, a test, and turning it on.
Your AI
Your own AI: what serves you now, your choices among what the team allows, your own accounts, the checks in force for you and what you have used.
AI for this project
The AIs this project uses, its budget and order, and the checks that apply to the work done directly in it.
When the AI can't go on
What the assistant shows when an account reaches its limit, a provider stops answering, a model is retired or material is about to go to a new provider.
Test an AI that isn't listed
Test a custom endpoint or an unlisted plan before it is used: the cost first, the result by part, and exactly what would be sent.
Results other teams sent
What other teams' tests found for each AI: the parts it passed, its limits, its speed and cost, and the grade.

Records one of the case's four details: the area of government, a point of contact, related work or relationships. It sits beside the case, the signature does not cover it, and you can change or clear it later.
Shows the four details of this case as they stand now, and who set each and when. None of them stops a case from being published.
Shows any reader the four details of this case as the team currently states them, with those it has not stated marked Not stated.

Re-weighs this case's findings under the lens you choose and shows which moved and which statement moved each. It saves nothing, changes nothing in the imported case and sends nothing to the source team.

Declares one of your team's projects a rerun of this edition, so you can compare your work with the original. It records only that; the imported case is not changed, nothing is accepted and nothing is sent to the source team.

States that one finding of this project answers the same claim as one of the original's, or withdraws that statement. It is your statement, kept in the history, and never changes either finding's strength.
Shows this rerun beside the original: the two lenses' differences and the findings you paired. It changes nothing.
Records, in your name, how two passages differ or which one is wrong. Neither passage is changed or removed.
Opens a question in the project from this contradiction, with both passages as its evidence, so the team can settle it and conclude.
Closes a lead with the reason you choose. It stays closed, and your name and reason are kept with it.
Concludes the question taken up from a contradiction and records what the contradiction turned out to be, in your name.
Tells the other projects that yours wants this conflict resolved. It cannot be taken back.
Sends your words to the other projects in the conflict, with only what you choose to share about yourself. It cannot be taken back.

Takes you to Cloudflare's own page to allow this installer into your account, then sets up your team's Civicsmith there under your short name, or updates it. The short name is permanent: it appears in every address and beside every signature.
Signs you in on this device with your handle and password, for as long as you chose. Several wrong tries pause sign-in from here for a while.
Unlocks this device with your password after it locked while you were away, and takes you back to where you were; nothing was lost. A wrong password counts as a refused sign-in.
Sets a new password with one of your recovery codes, for any member. The code is spent, and every other sign-in of yours ends.
Sets the languages your team's members use: Civicsmith's own words are shown in each, and members choose among them when they join. The places whose rules apply are not changed.
Replaces the logo shown beside your team's name on its page, its masthead and its published cases. A logo is optional; with none, the name stands alone.
Sets your new password from the reset link an administrator made for you. The link is spent, every other sign-in of yours ends, and your handle and work stay as they are.
Signs you out on this device. Your work stays in your team's Civicsmith.
Signs you out on every phone and computer you are signed in on, this one included.
Starts joining through the team's join link: the name the team will know you by, then your handle and password.
Makes a one-time link for this member to choose a new password, valid for seven days. You send it yourself; Civicsmith sends no email. Their other sign-ins end when they use it.

Lists the people and organizations your team's record follows: each with its role or office, how many documents, questions and projects name it and when the newest was added, those your projects touch first. A read: it changes nothing.
Makes you the team's first administrator, using the one-time password from installing. Until it is claimed, nobody can use the team's Civicsmith.
Sets the name members and readers see. It can be changed later; the short name cannot.
Proves your team controls this web address, so published cases can show it as yours.
Chooses the places whose rules apply (deadlines, records laws, holidays) and the team's languages. Deadlines and wizards draw on these.
Lists the public offices and seats for your places, so requests and people can be addressed by role.
Confirms an office that a member named, so it no longer carries the mark Named by a member. Only an administrator can.
Adds something the record does not hold yet, such as an office, an organization or a court case, with a note on where it comes from.
Names a place Civicsmith does not yet hold rules for. Administrators are told when an update brings it.
Keeps the team's material away from AI, for every use or the ones you choose. It binds every account, the team's, any project's and members' own. Members see your reason on Settings › The assistant.
Holds one Anthropic API key for the team, sealed and never shown again. It pays for a member's act when neither a project's account nor the member's own serves it.
Turns the team's key on or off without removing it. Members who rely on it are told what changed.
Chooses whether members are told, when they join and the first time they record something not public, what a court order could reach.
Records who holds the Cloudflare account. Whoever holds it can reach everything, so the team should know who that is.

Takes you to the update page for the Civicsmith already in this account, set to the newest release. Its records, members and settings are kept, and nothing changes until you allow it on Cloudflare's page.
Installs a second Civicsmith in this same account, for another team, under its own short name and address. The one already here is not touched, and neither can read the other's records.
Registers the address you chose for your Cloudflare account: the name every program in the account answers under, your team's Civicsmith included.
Keeps your team's record in the region you choose instead of near you, for a team bound by a law or an agreement on where its record is kept.

Looks at your Cloudflare account and tells you, line by line, what is ready and what is not: the account, the plan, R2 storage, containers, room under your account's limits, the account's address, the permission you gave, the short name, a payment card and the size of each part. It creates nothing that stays in your account, and you can run it as often as you like.
Opens a page that lists everything the Civicsmith already here holds, all of which removing it would delete. Nothing is deleted on that page until you confirm there.
Deletes the Civicsmith already in this account, with every record, document and member account it holds, then goes on with your new installation. It cannot be undone, by you or by anyone.
Opens the installer's update page for your team, set to the release you chose and no other. Nothing changes until whoever holds the team's Cloudflare account allows it there.
Puts this release aside for every administrator. It comes back later, the next day for a security fix, and at once when a newer release replaces it.
Says your team will not install this release, with your reason kept on the record for every administrator to see. The next release is offered as usual.
Adds a security tool your organization uses. Before it is turned on you see what it is sent, who receives it and how long it keeps files.
Creates an invitation for one person, under the cover the team knows them by. Nothing about them is public.
Saves what your team is, what it focuses on and why, and who may see each part: members only, or also the public.
Asks the assistant for a draft of your team's description, labeled as its draft. Nothing is saved until you keep it.
Shows who invited you, to which team, and what joining means, before you decide.
Sets the language Civicsmith speaks to you. Documents stay in their own language.
Joins the team with a handle and password. Your handle is how members see you; it need not be your name.
Starts from where you are: a problem you live with, a document, a deadline, a claim to check or a person. Each opens the right first step.
Changes what a member may do: contribute, administer. The change is recorded with who made it.
Changes a member's status, for example to inactive. Their past work stays in the record under their handle.
Adds your endorsement to make a member an administrator. With one administrator the team depends on one person.
Removes an administrator's powers, with a reason. It cannot leave the team with none.
Takes a copy of the team's whole working record, with checksums to verify it later, and adds it to the list of copies. It cannot be undone, and every administrator can read the list.
Shows the copies of the record taken so far, newest first, each with its time, counts and the words given.
Chooses whether your cover name and your handle are published together. You and any administrator can change it later.
Checks that the team's record answers and that stored files can be written and read back. It changes nothing for the team.
Shows how much work the copy's requests have done, to see how close it runs to Cloudflare's limits. It changes nothing.
Confirms a member's declared expertise, so it can be asked for when a check needs it.
Withdraws a confirmed expertise, with your reason. It can no longer be asked for, and the history keeps who confirmed and who withdrew it.
Cancels an invitation nobody has used yet. The link stops working at once.
Creates a key that lets your team's website invite people, through an open form or an application someone approves.
Turns on one reusable link anyone with it can use to ask to join. You can turn it off at any time.
Removes the team's key for good. Members without their own account use Civicsmith without the assistant.
Shows how hard your team's Civicsmith was tried over the period you choose, against its usual. Counts only.
Sends a harmless test file or address to the tool and shows its answer, so you know it works before relying on it.
Stops using this tool. Notes it already wrote stay on the files they concern.
Asks your team's file scanner to check for new signatures now. It answers at once, and the result shows when the check has finished. No document is moved.
Says what you know professionally, such as accounting or law. An administrator confirms it; members can then ask you for checks.
Changes your password. Every other session signed in as you ends, so anyone using an old one must sign in again with the new password.
Tells the project's owners, in their queues, that this edition is prepared and ready to sign. It signs nothing.
Withdraws a member's signing key, for a lost or stolen device. It stops working at once; what it already signed can still be checked.
Makes your signing key in this browser and registers its public half with your team, so readers can check what you sign. Civicsmith never sees the key.
Withdraws your signing key, for example if it was lost. Cases already signed keep a record that it was withdrawn.
Chooses how quickly explanations open: promptly, or guidance on a longer pause so less opens while you move. Nothing is ever hidden.
Confirms you have read that your questions go to Anthropic under the team's account. Asked once, before your first question.
Confirms you have read what connecting your own account means: your questions go to Anthropic under your own account and terms.
Opens Anthropic's own sign-in page in a new tab, then connects your subscription with the code it gives you. Civicsmith never sees your password, and the code is used once and never kept.
Disconnects your Claude subscription from your team's Civicsmith. The team's key serves you instead, if the team has one.
Connects your own Claude API key. It serves only you, before the team's key, and Anthropic bills you for each use.
Disconnects your own API key and removes it from your team's Civicsmith. The team's key serves you instead, if the team has one.
Lists a tie that could matter to a case: an employer, a relative in a public body, a business interest. A case that concerns it says so.
Removes a tie from your list. A case already published keeps what it said.
Writes a note only you can see. Use it for thoughts not ready for the team.
Turns your note into something the team shares: an observation, a hunch or a question. The note itself stays private.
Changes your note. Notes are yours alone, so nothing else changes.
Deletes your note. If you turned it into something shared, that stays.

Asks the assistant to draft the case's account in the order you chose, from the case's own findings and evidence. Its draft arrives labeled as machine work, with the sentences Civicsmith could not support marked; the account stays the one you write.
Lists the project's drafts of the case, each named by its scope and the date it was prepared, the newest marked.
Lists every draft the assistant made of this case's account, oldest first, each with how it was ordered and what Civicsmith marked.
Asks the assistant to help word what you are writing, from what you typed. Its words arrive labeled as its draft; nothing is saved until you keep them.
Asks the assistant to draft translations of Civicsmith's words, labeled as drafts for a speaker to check.
Keeps a translation so members reading that language see it. Protected words need a second speaker's check first.
Lets a named member translate Civicsmith's words into one language.
Confirms a protected word as a second speaker, so members see it instead of the English.
Undoes a translation change in one step, back to what it replaced.
Shows the wizards your team can use: Civicsmith's, and those your team wrote.
Records a new wizard by walking through the steps yourself. It stays a draft until approved.
Changes a draft wizard's steps or words before it is submitted.
Submits a draft wizard for an administrator to approve before members are offered it.
Approves a wizard so members are offered it where its steps start.
Stops offering a wizard. Anyone part-way through can finish.
Marks this item done where nothing more is asked of you, and it leaves your queue. An item that needs you to read, check or decide has its own button for that, and stays until you have.

Records, in your name, who issued this document, or that you looked and could not tell, with your reason. The task is done and leaves the list. A later answer replaces it, and the earlier one stays in the history.
Passes this item to another member better placed to act.
Dismisses a suggestion or hint with a reason, kept on the record so the same thing is not raised again without cause.
Hides the item, and the other items in its case, until the date you choose, when they come back.
Stops this kind of item, or a project's items, reaching your queue, or lets muted ones reach it again. What you muted is listed under Muted at the foot of your queue.
Asks the record whether a newer copy of this document exists, for one question that rests on it. The answer is yes, no, or not established; nothing moves until you adopt or keep.
Sets two revisions of this copy's record side by side and marks what differs. It changes nothing.
Copies this fingerprint to your clipboard, so you can check the copy elsewhere or quote it. It changes nothing.
Opens the outside address in a new window after the warning. What is there is not part of your team's record, and nothing you see there is vouched for by it.
Moves your citations to the newer version of this document. You see what changed first.
Keeps citing the version you cited. The newer one stays in the record beside it.
Answers a reminder you set, for example that a reply came or a deadline passed.
Turns what you are looking at into something the team will work on: a hint, chain or suggestion into a question, or a problem into a project. Where it came from is kept with it.
Searches everything your team holds that you may see: documents, passages, questions, people.
Holds the items you picked together so one act can apply to them all. The set is held until the time shown.
Looks inside these documents for people, money figures, dates, requirements or a word. Each result shows its passage; nothing is recorded until you record it.
Lets the held set go. Nothing in it changes.
Shows where nobody has looked yet for this, so the team knows what an answer does not cover.
Has your team's Civicsmith fetch this address itself and keep exactly what the site sent, with when and from where. Progress and the result show on the page.
Adds this file or photo to the record, with who made or obtained it and how. It waits in Held captures until vouched for.
Records what you saw or heard yourself as testimony: grade D, labeled as yours, never changed afterwards.
Asks for this to be captured later, for example when a site is down. The request waits until it can be fetched.
Lists the requests you asked for later, each with where it stands: waiting, being fetched, captured, turned away or expired. It changes nothing.
Checks this address once, now, for a new version. Offered only for an address your team is watching. A new version is kept beside the old.
Gives you ten new one-time recovery codes for your own role, shown to you once, and spends every earlier unused one. Nobody else can see or use them.
Turns watching on or off for this document's address, and sets how often it is checked. Each new version found is kept beside the old, and you are told.
Shows captures waiting for a member to vouch for them before they count.
Vouches that each copy is what its source gave, unaltered. It is signed with your name; it can be corrected later, never silently undone.
Sets the picked captures aside with one reason, shown to anyone waiting on them. They can be restored.
Brings a set-aside capture back, with a reason, so it can be vouched for.
Explains this copy's grade: how it was obtained and what would raise it.
Lists the archive's files by state: filed, already held, or not filed and why.
Opens the original file on your device. A low-risk file is checked first if its last check is over a week old.
Opens a high-risk original on your own device without a deeper check, after you confirm you will not enable macros or editing.
Shows the safe copy on this page, without downloading anything: each page as a picture, or a spreadsheet's figures as data. Nothing in it can run. Cite the original, not this.
Runs every check on this file: read whole, the built-in scanner again, and your team's outside tools. A clean result opens the original to everyone for 24 hours.
Gives your reason to release a file a scanner flagged. A second member's reason releases it; the machine never can.
Cites this passage in a question, as support or as cutting against it. A citation always points at the original document.
Adds a name documents use for them, or takes one off with your reason. Civicsmith then looks for the name in the documents your team holds; a shared name never decides which one a document means.
Declares a tie between two people or organizations the record follows, with why and where it is said. It reads “declared, not evidenced” until a source that states it is attached.
Has Civicsmith match this document's mention to them, by an identifier or the name, and grade the match. A stronger match raises the grade; a match never falls.
Records from your own knowledge that this mention is them, with how you know. It is your word, grade D: never established on its own, and never lowering a stronger match.
Joins the documents that name them, pair by pair, each connection graded by the weaker of the two matches. Civicsmith also does this on its own as documents arrive.
Asks the assistant for options on this plan. It opens one planning run; the options it finds wait in the tray, labeled as its work, until a member adopts one. Nothing in the plan changes by asking.
Backs a step someone declared with a passage of a document your team holds that states it. The step then rests on evidence, graded like the document it cites.
Takes back a source you attached to a declared step, with your reason. The step goes back to resting on someone's word, and the earlier source stays in its history.
Records that a reply asks not to be quoted, in the reply's own words, or takes that record back. The case can still say what the reply says, never in its words.

Shows this in the language you read, translated by a machine for you alone and marked as machine work; passages it quotes stay in their own words. Nothing is saved: the original stays the record, one tap away, and you quote only the original.
Shows the proceeding's own dates and your team's deadlines on it, as two lanes side by side. It says when things are due; it never says anyone is late.
Shows administrators the release your team runs, when it last checked for a new one, and any release ready to install, with its notes.
Shows how much of the assistant an account has used, day by day, against each of its limits, to the people who pay for it.
Draws what the record joins to one person, organization or document, two steps out, with how strong each connection is.
Lists the standards proposed in this project and what became of each: adopted, set aside, or still open.
Shows a prepared text exactly as it was saved, so leaving the page between preparing and approving loses nothing.
Shows the pressure your team has put on an action or project: what was done, when, and what came of it.
Remembers when you last looked at Home, so Home can show what happened since.

Stores the login you type for this source, sealed, and then puts the turned-away request back in the queue to be tried again. The password or secret is never shown again, and a machine cannot give one.
Puts a request the source itself turned away back in the queue to be tried again, with what your team holds for that source. Any other request is left as it is.
Lists the sources your team has stored a login for, and who gave each, with the date. It never shows a username or a secret.
Destroys the stored login for this source. Requests to it are turned away for a login again until someone gives a new one.
Records, with your name and the date, the system this document came from. A second declaration is added beside the first and never replaces it. The document itself does not change.
Sets a passage here beside a passage in another document as a contradiction your project settles, with your reason. It changes neither document.

Rests one of your team's questions on a finding your team accepted from another team's case, at the edition shown. It carries the fact that they published it, and the grade the edition published, never higher.
Takes another team's finding off this question's answer, with your reason. The history keeps it, and so does each version already frozen.
Lists the requests to gather something on a schedule that you may see, with where each is looked for, when it was last tried and when it is next due.
Opens another view of the item you are on, such as the money it is tied to or the events it took part in, already narrowed to it. You do not start over, and nothing is recorded.

Lists every connection found between the two ends within the search's limits, each with its steps, its weakest step and its dates. It says when the search was cut short, and never that the list is complete.
Shows the most direct chain between the two ends first: the fewest steps, then the strongest weakest step, then the date. It is a fact about the chains, not a judgment.
Puts paths with fewer steps between the same two ends beside the one you built, evidenced paths first and then leads, so you can see them or keep your own. Your chain is never changed.

Brings in a whole public register as one capture, with its source and the date, and reads it in the background. Your team is told in the queue when it is ready. It never keeps a home address or a phone number.
Lists the registers your team holds, with where each came from, when it was brought in, how many rows it has and when it is next checked.
Looks through the registers your team holds for a person or an organization, an amount or a date. It records nothing.
Cites one row of a register as evidence, with the register, its source and the date it was brought in.
Watches one named filer, license or docket by its number, and tells your team once in the queue when it changes. It never watches a person.

Chooses which rows of a register to bring in, by names, organizations, amounts, dates or filer numbers. It starts from what the project you are in is interested in, and you can change it. Leave it empty to bring in the whole register.
Shows what bringing in would add to your record before anything is brought in: the new rows, the bytes, and about how long it takes. It changes nothing.
Reads a register ahead for the team, whole or in the part you chose, as a resource before any project asks. It runs by fixed steps and never uses the assistant.
Proposes a register we know that is not in the list, by its name, its address and who publishes it. Nothing is brought in.
Keeps looking for connections after the explorer stopped at 2 seconds, and adds what it finds to what is shown. It never says the list is complete.
Stops watching one filer, license or docket. What was brought in stays in the record.
Connects an outside service that sends an alert when a watched item changes, with your team's own key for it. The key is sealed and never shown again.
Answers a question asked in plain words across the registers your team holds. It comes after the alpha, with the assistant.
Proposes matches between names in a register and your team's subjects, for a member to accept or reject. It comes after the alpha, with the assistant.
Proposes filers, licenses or dockets worth watching, for a member to accept or decline. It comes after the alpha, with the assistant.
Opens the guided connection for this plan: what it is sent, how to sign up, how to give the key, a test and then turning it on. Nothing is connected until you finish.
Opens the test for an AI no release lists yet. It shows what the test costs before it runs and what would be sent afterward.
Opens the results other teams sent about the AIs they tested: the parts each passed, its limits, and how fast and costly it was.
Moves this account one place up or down in the order. Work goes to the first account that is on, allowed for that work and within its limits.
Switches this account off or on. Work stays refused on a use that is off; it is never moved to another account.
Removes this account from your team's list. Its key is deleted from Cloudflare's store, and what it cost stays in the history.
Sets a monthly budget for one account or for all of them, and the percentage at which administrators are told.
Chooses which of the seven privacy and origin checks the whole team requires. A required check is locked for project owners and members.
Chooses which providers, plans and models members may use, and whether they may add accounts of their own.
Sends the key straight to Cloudflare's AI Gateway store in your team's own account. Civicsmith keeps no copy, and the key is never shown again.
Records that you entered the key yourself in Cloudflare's dashboard. Civicsmith then checks that it works, without ever holding the key.
Takes you to the provider's own page to sign in and approve the connection. Civicsmith never sees your password.
Saves where the key is kept, not the key. Civicsmith asks for it from there each time it is needed.
Records, with your name and the date, that you accepted the terms that bind your team's use of this plan, and any warning it carried.
Sends a harmless test message that holds none of your team's material, and reports whether the connection works. The account stays off until the test passes.
Turns the connected account on and puts it in the place you chose in the order. It cannot be turned on before its test passes.
Records your choice to use your own subscription for your own work, within the provider's stated restrictions. It is never the team's or a project's account.
Chooses which provider, plan, model and effort serve the work you start, among what your team allows.
Opens the guided connection so you can add an account of your own, where your team allows it.
Requires, for your own work, a check your team has left open. An AI that fails it is not used for your work, and you are told why.
Narrows which of the team's AIs this project uses. A project can use fewer, never more.
Sets a monthly budget for this project's AI use.
Moves an AI up or down in this project's order, within the team's.
Requires a check, a project owner's choice, for all work done directly in this project. The checks the team requires stay locked.
Lets this answer continue on the next account in the order. Nothing continues on another account until you say so.
Stops the answer where it is. Nothing more is sent to any provider.
Sends the material to this provider for the first time, as the notice described. The step waited for you.
Keeps the material here and sends nothing to this provider.
Waits until the limit resets or the provider answers again. Nothing is sent meanwhile.
Carries on without the assistant. Your question and your work are kept.
Sends this answer to another account that is allowed for this work. The switch is shown and recorded.
Uses the model you choose in place of the retired one for this work.
Opens the choice of another AI that has passed this part of the assistant's work.
Asks the administrator who switched this use off to switch it back on. It is sent to their queue; nothing else changes.
Starts the run on the account named, at about the cost shown. The cost afterward is shown when it ends.
Chooses another allowed account for this run before it starts.
Saves the endpoint and key for the test. The key is sealed and never shown again.
Runs Civicsmith's standard test against the endpoint, part by part, and stops before it passes the spend ceiling you set.
Sends the sealed results bundle shown above to the library of results other teams read. It holds no test conversation, and your team's name only if you ticked it.
Keeps the results here and sends nothing.
Shows the results other teams sent for one AI, or for every AI.
Saves one request to gather something from the places you name, and how often to look, or retires it. It fetches nothing by itself.
Saves a sweep: the sites it may visit, the pages it starts from, what it keeps, how often it runs and the most it may fetch. It does not run until the project's owner ratifies it.
The project's owner starts a sweep, or any member who can write to the project stops it. Ratifying sends your team's fetches to the named sites, within the scope and budget shown.
Closes this project now, whether or not its work has gone quiet, with the reason you choose and an optional note. What was still open at the close is kept beside the reason. An owner can reopen it.

Records what the team has at stake in this project beyond its usual stake. It goes beside the team's statement on what this project sends or publishes, dated and attributed; clearing it leaves the team's statement alone.

Records what the team has at stake in this one action beyond its usual stake and the project's. It goes beside them on what the action sends, dated and attributed; clearing it falls back to the project's stake.
Sets the handle you sign in with from now on, once: the name the record shows on your work. Until you choose, you sign in as admin.

Switches the project between hidden (only its members know it exists) and findable (every member of the team sees it in Projects and can ask to join), with a reason kept in its history. Only an owner changes it.
Makes a member an owner. With one owner, that owner decides alone; with two or more, every owner agrees, each by making the same change.
Shows exactly what your notice would say and what your key would sign, and writes nothing. Used again to change the notice or to stop it.
Signs the previewed notice with your key and publishes it at your team's address. Stopping it later does not unsay it.
Ends someone's ownership, with a reason; they stay a member. A project always keeps at least one owner, and with three or more owners the others agree first.
Takes a member off the project, with a reason they see. Their work on it stays, under their name.
Tells the owners you are leaving the project, with a note if you like. An owner can leave once another owner remains.
Starts a new project of your own from this one, with you as its only owner and the visibility you choose.
Makes an administrator an owner of a project whose owners are all gone, with a reason on its record. Never for a project a member kept for themselves alone.
Puts what you picked on your watch list: Find shows it under Watched by you, and a change to it reaches your queue. Only you see what you watch.
Asks the team to look at what you picked again, with a note saying why. It shows under Flagged for a second look until a member clears the flag.
Takes the flag off. No reason is asked; any member who can see the item may clear it.
Corrects your team's time zone: choose it by name and say how and where you checked it. Dates and deadlines are counted in it from then on.
Takes off a name you added for them, with your reason. Documents that use only that name are no longer matched to them by it.
Sets how carefully the team should act on this, from 1 (file freely) to 3 (do not file without counsel), with a reason kept in its history. Only a member sets it.
Puts a law beside the one chosen, for a member to weigh. It changes nothing until a member chooses it.
Opens a question with this action carried as its reference. You write the question; the action is where it comes from, not evidence in it.

Records, for each passage this question cites, whether your answer falls if that passage turns out wrong, or still holds because of other passages you cite.
